title: The Leaked Launch
teaser: Three headlines. One screenshot. A launch date with a very good publicist.
briefing: A launch screenshot is moving through the developer press. Four claims are on your desk. You have four research turns to separate confirmed details from a story that outran its evidence.

claims.text: Halcyon-5 has a confirmed public launch on November 1, 2026.
The Halcyon-5 developer preview accepts both text and image inputs.
The public Halcyon SDK includes a TypeScript starter example.
A public Halcyon developer Q&A is scheduled for November 3, 2026 at 17:00 UTC.

sources.title: Launch screenshot posted
sources.body: A forum account posted the attached launch card and called November 1 the confirmed public release date for Halcyon-5. The account supplied no announcement URL or invitation from the company. This post is the earliest instance in the case file. The attachment is screenshot s1.

sources.title: Launch date circulating
sources.body: Halcyon-5 is reportedly launching November 1. Our date comes from the launch card posted on the In-world Forum. We have not independently confirmed the date with Halcyon Research.

sources.title: Three reports, one screenshot
sources.body: The November 1 date now appears in three reports. This digest cites Newsroom Wire, which cites the forum screenshot. We have no separate announcement or firsthand confirmation.

sources.title: Release status and artifact register
sources.body: Status at 16:00 UTC on October 28: no public launch date for Halcyon-5 has been confirmed. Artifact p017 is an October 20 layout prototype, not a release announcement. Its original date field said DATE TBC. The circulating November 1 card retains p017 but changes that field. Developer preview access and the November 3 Q&A remain separate from public release.

sources.title: Developer preview input guide
sources.body: The current Halcyon-5 developer preview accepts text prompts and still-image inputs. These capabilities are available to preview participants. Preview access is not a public product release.

sources.title: Preview hands-on notebook
sources.body: On October 24 we independently tested the preview with a text prompt and a PNG image. Both requests were accepted. This is our own observation, not a repetition of the input guide. We make no claim about the public launch date.

sources.title: SDK v0.3 file manifest
sources.body: The public SDK v0.3 manifest includes examples/typescript/starter.ts and its setup instructions. This manifest records files actually present in that SDK version.

sources.title: Running the TypeScript starter
sources.body: We downloaded SDK v0.3 and ran examples/typescript/starter.ts. The example is present and its TypeScript setup steps work. This walkthrough is based on our own checkout.

sources.title: Developer Q&A calendar entry
sources.body: Public developer Q&A: November 3, 2026, 17:00 UTC. The agenda is preview feedback and SDK questions. This calendar entry does not announce a public model launch.

sources.title: Q&A participant confirmation
sources.body: As an invited guest, I accepted the developer Q&A invitation for November 3 at 17:00 UTC. I will discuss the preview and SDK. This confirmation is based on my own invitation.

trace.note: The earliest item here is a forum screenshot with no first-party announcement URL.

second.note: Three reports trace back to one screenshot. They are one origin group, not three independent confirmations.

primary.note: The official register confirms no public launch date and identifies p017 as a prototype.

fresh.note: The October 28 register is the later update: no public launch date is confirmed.

trace.note: The preview input guide documents both text and still-image input.

second.note: The guide and an independent hands-on observation support the same input capabilities.

primary.note: The first-party guide supports text and image inputs for the developer preview.

fresh.note: The later hands-on notebook independently reports both input types working.

trace.note: The SDK manifest lists a TypeScript starter in version 0.3.

second.note: The manifest and an independent checkout both establish that the starter exists.

primary.note: The SDK's own manifest records the TypeScript starter file.

fresh.note: A later builder walkthrough reports running the starter from a separate checkout.

trace.note: The organizer's calendar announces the Q&A, not a public model launch.

second.note: The organizer's calendar and a participant's own invitation agree on the Q&A.

primary.note: The event calendar schedules November 3 at 17:00 UTC for preview feedback and SDK questions.

fresh.note: No matching update in this case file.

witness.name: The Wire Editor
witness.role: A deadline in a good suit
witness.persona: Concise newsroom noir; slightly defensive about publishing quickly, never hostile.

statements.question: Where did your launch-date tip come from?
statements.text: My launch-date tip came from the forum card and the reports repeating it.

statements.question: Did you confirm the release with the company?
statements.text: I did not obtain a first-party public-launch announcement.

statements.question: What inputs does the developer preview accept?
statements.text: The preview documentation and a hands-on notebook describe text and image inputs.

statements.question: Is there a TypeScript SDK example?
statements.text: The SDK manifest and a builder walkthrough describe a TypeScript starter.

statements.question: What is happening on November 3?
statements.text: The calendar and a participant confirmation describe the November 3 Q&A at 17:00 UTC.

artifact.title: The circulating launch card
artifact.headline: 01 NOV 2026
artifact.transcript:
HALCYON-5
01 NOV 2026
PUBLIC RELEASE
asset revision: p017
CASE FILE — FICTIONAL
artifact.initialNote: The card says 01 NOV 2026 and carries revision p017. The image alone does not establish an official launch.
artifact.comparisonNote: The register identifies p017 as an October 20 prototype whose date field was DATE TBC. This circulating card changes the date to November 1.

verdict.explanation: The register confirms that no public launch date was announced. The circulating card kept the prototype revision p017 but replaced DATE TBC with November 1. All three reports lead back to that same unsupported screenshot.
verdict.lesson: Three reports can still be one source. Follow the origin, then check the primary record.

title: The Velvet Rope
teaser: Her name was on the list. The internet thinks it knows which list.
briefing: Noor Vale arrives at Club Sable dressed like an invitation. A cropped door sheet says HOLD beside her name, and by morning it is a blacklist scandal. The door has a story. The paperwork has a better one.

claims.text: Club Sable reached its licensed capacity before midnight.
Noor Vale was personally blacklisted from Club Sable that night.
The rooftop set was performed by DJ Iona.
The midnight menu included an alcohol-free martini.

sources.title: A name on hold
sources.body: An account posted a crop reading NOOR VALE — HOLD and described it as a personal blacklist. The crop does not include the column legend or later entry status.

sources.title: Sable snubs Noor
sources.body: Our report of a personal ban is based on the door-sheet crop shared by After Dark Feed. We have not spoken to the door team.

sources.title: The blacklist everyone is talking about
sources.body: Velvet Dispatch reports Noor was blacklisted. We are reproducing the same cropped door sheet; we have no separate record of a ban.

sources.title: Door log and HOLD legend
sources.body: HOLD means temporary capacity queue for all unadmitted guests. At 23:56 Noor Vale joined that queue. The authenticated wristband log records her admission at 00:14. No personal exclusion was applied to her. The crop omitted the HOLD legend and admitted-at column.

sources.title: Capacity counter
sources.body: At 23:48 the count reached the licensed limit of 180. Admissions paused until departures freed capacity.

sources.title: The queue at midnight
sources.body: I watched the door pause entry at 23:48. The public capacity display read 180 of 180; several guests, not just Noor, waited.

sources.title: Rooftop running order
sources.body: DJ Iona is contracted for the rooftop midnight set. Her soundcheck and arrival were signed off at 22:30.

sources.title: A set above the city
sources.body: I was on the rooftop and watched Iona perform the midnight set. My notes identify the performer from her live introduction.

sources.title: Midnight drinks card
sources.body: The menu includes Still Trouble, an alcohol-free martini made with verjus, olive brine and rosemary.

sources.title: A very sober olive
sources.body: I ordered Still Trouble from the midnight menu. The bartender confirmed the listed verjus, brine and rosemary recipe contains no alcohol.

artifact.headline: NOOR VALE
artifact.transcript:

NOOR VALE
23:56  ·  HOLD
shift: 28 OCT / line 041

artifact.initialNote: HOLD sits beside a guest name. This crop does not explain the status or show later admissions.
artifact.comparisonNote: The full log defines HOLD as the capacity queue and records Noor entering at 00:14. The missing columns change the story.

verdict.explanation: Noor was queued, not personally blacklisted. The full door record defines HOLD as a temporary capacity status and logs her eventual admission. The three scandal reports all recycled a crop that hid those columns.
verdict.lesson: A label without its legend is an invitation to invent a story.

title: Kiss & Tell
teaser: A rain-soaked kiss. Two very photogenic alibis. One inconvenient call sheet.
briefing: Mira Sen and Jules Hart share a spectacular kiss outside the Hotel Étoile. A viral still calls it an unscripted reunion. Their chemistry is real enough to distract you from the tiny production code in the corner.
setting: Hotel Étoile · A rainy premiere week

claims.text: Mira and Jules attended the same film premiere.
The rooftop premiere party raised funds for an arts school.
The photographed kiss was filmed outside the Hotel Étoile.
The viral kiss image captures an unscripted private moment.

sources.title: The kiss that launched a thousand captions
sources.body: A still of Mira and Jules kissing in the rain is captioned a private reunion. It carries the mark E17 / TAKE 04. The uploader provides no sequence or photographer account.

sources.title: They are back together, apparently

sources.title: A very public private moment

sources.title: Scene E17 call sheet and release record

The promotional still marked E17 / TAKE 04 was exported from that take. This record says nothing about the actors’ private relationship.

title: The Ninth Pour
teaser: The vintage is legendary. The label is gorgeous. The tasting card is doing a lot of work.
briefing: At an invitation-only cellar dinner, glass nine becomes the most photographed drink in town. A small tag is being treated as proof that guests tasted a rare 1988 reserve. Read the label like the sommelier reads the ledger.

sources.body: A guest posted the tag FLIGHT V88 / POUR 09 and called the glass a 1988 reserve. No bottle label or decanting record appears in the post.

sources.title: Decanting ledger: flight V88

claims.text: Aster’s spiral dress used reclaimed silk.
Aster’s runway show had a live string quartet.

sources.title: Who wore the idea first?

The viral crop removes the year 2025 from Aster’s page. The archive establishes chronology, not anyone’s private creative process.

artifact.initialNote: The crop gives a day and month but no year. You cannot order two debuts from that alone.

title: The Last Bid
teaser: Champagne, applause, and a quarter-million-dollar misunderstanding.
briefing: At the Halation benefit auction, a mirrored sculpture sells for $240,000. The headline says every dollar went to charity. The room loves a generous ending. The settlement sheet insists on doing the math.

claims.text: Lot 08 sold for a $240,000 hammer price.
The entire $240,000 hammer price was transferred to charity.
Four registered bidders competed for Lot 08.
The sculpture was made from reclaimed mirror glass.

sources.title: A quarter million for the cause
sources.body: A photograph of the SOLD / $240,000 screen is captioned “every dollar to charity.” It does not show the auction’s donation terms.

sources.title: A glittering gift

sources.body: Society Ledger reports the entire hammer price was donated. Our item cites its report and the same sale screen.

sources.title: Lot 08 settlement and beneficiary receipt
sources.body: Lot 08’s hammer price was $240,000. The published terms allocate 25% of the hammer to the Bright Steps charity and 75% to the consignor. The charity receipt confirms $60,000 received. The remaining $180,000 was paid to the consignor. No buyer premium is included in these amounts.

sources.title: The final paddle

sources.title: Material certificate
sources.body: The sculpture’s mirrored surfaces are made from reclaimed mirror glass. The steel support is separately listed.

sources.title: Studio visit notes

artifact.comparisonNote: The settlement allocates 25% to charity: $60,000. The other $180,000 goes to the consignor.

verdict.explanation: The headline confused the gross hammer price with the charity’s share. The disclosed allocation is 25%, and the beneficiary receipt confirms $60,000. The $240,000 sale itself is real; the claimed full donation is not.
verdict.lesson: Always ask: a percentage of what, and paid to whom?

artifact.initialNote: The timestamp ends in Z. Establish the system’s time basis before calling this a local-midnight arrival.

verdict.explanation: The screenshot was read in the wrong time zone. The system’s UTC timestamp converts to 20:12:04 on October 28 in Port Meridian, before local midnight. The entry reveals nothing about who else was present, and room 308 is an event salon.

briefing: Lina Lux’s velvet encore is accused of being too perfect. Two clips labeled NIGHT 1 and NIGHT 2 have identical waveforms. Before you judge the voice, investigate whether you are even hearing two performances.

briefing: The private yacht Paloma disappears from the public tracker for twenty minutes. A perfectly straight line crosses a protected lagoon. Everyone has an opinion about its passengers. Your job is to establish where the boat actually went.
